# playwright-release-confidence

Playwright and TypeScript tests for
[Restful-Booker-Platform](https://github.com/mwinteringham/restful-booker-platform) (RBP), a
bed-and-breakfast booking app made for testing practice. They check its REST API, the pages a
visitor uses and its admin area, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. A release gate then decides
whether a build may ship.

## What the suite covers

| Area | Tests | Known bugs (expected to fail) | Runs in |

| Admin area | 11 | 0 | chromium, firefox, webkit |
| Booking | 6 | 2 | chromium, firefox, webkit |

| Honest signals | 17 | 0 | meta |
| **All** | **90** | **7** | 146 runs across projects |
<!-- numbers:end -->

The full list, with the reason for each test: [TEST-CASES.md](TEST-CASES.md). A known bug is a real
defect found while exploring the app. Its test checks for the right behaviour and is marked as
expected to fail, with a link to its
[issue](https://github.com/TalhaAhmedMubashir/playwright-release-confidence/issues?q=label%3Aknown-bug):
the suite stays green while the bug is visible, and the gate turns red the day it is fixed.

## How it works

- **The app** runs from pinned images (`docker-compose.yml`). Every CI job starts its own copy,
  in about 1.5 minutes ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md), decision 1).
- **Selectors** come only from what exploring the app recorded
  ([docs/exploration](docs/exploration)), never from guesses.
- **Test data** is made through the API for each test and deleted by name afterwards: each test
  that books gets a room of its own, so tests never collide and can run in parallel.
- **The guard:** a test that changes what every visitor sees runs only with
  `ALLOW_SITE_SETTINGS_CHANGES=1`, and must leave the site as it found it (`src/guard.ts`).
- **Honest signals:** lint stops tests that can't fail; CI fails if a test file is never
  collected or if the numbers above stop matching the tests; and self-tests prove each of these
  checks can fail.
- **CI:** every pull request runs lint, types, the honest-signal checks, a secret scan, the API
  tests and the UI smoke tests, then the release gate. Every night the whole suite runs in all three
  browsers, with accessibility checks, and the gate judges the merged result.

More: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) (how the code is laid out), [STRATEGY.md](STRATEGY.md)
(what is tested where, and why), [LIMITATIONS.md](LIMITATIONS.md) (what this suite doesn't prove).

## Run it

Needs Docker with the compose plugin, and Node 24.

```sh
npm ci
npx playwright install --with-deps
npm run app:start        # pulls and starts the app, then waits until every service answers
npm test                 # the full suite, as at night
npm run test:pr          # what a pull request runs
npm run gate             # the release gate's verdict on the last run
npm run app:stop
```

Checks that need neither the app nor a browser: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`,
`npm run test:meta`, `npm run check:collected`, `npm run readme:check`.

The tests run only against a copy of the app on this machine: any other address stops the run
(`src/config.ts`).
